interface_detail: a .gitlab-ci.yml pipeline; a runner with a shell
tooling: a shell on an ephemeral runner; package managers; a checkout
chaining: a real machine for the length of a job and nothing after it

limits.value: 400 compute minutes a month on the Free tier, with a cost factor of 1 on the default `small` Linux x86-64 runner, 2 on `medium`, 3 on `large`, 6 on `xlarge`, 12 on `2xlarge`
'Jobs handled by hosted runners on GitLab.com time out after 3 hours, regardless of the timeout configured in a project.'
'Inbound communication from the public internet to the ephemeral VM is not allowed.' Firewall rules 'only allow outbound communication from the ephemeral VM to the public internet'.

A card gates the free minutes. Quoted: 'credit/debit card details are required if you choose to use GitLab.com shared runners. Credit/debit card details are not required if you bring your own runner or disable shared runners.' Verified by 'a one-dollar authorization transaction. No charge will be made and no money will transfer.'
On quota exhaustion, instance runners stop processing new jobs; running jobs continue until the namespace is over quota by 1,000 compute minutes, then they are dropped

limits_note: Three separate ceilings and the smallest is the card gate: 400 compute minutes a month, a 3-hour job timeout, and a card required to use the shared runners that the minutes are spent on. Bringing your own runner removes the card requirement and the minute quota at the same time, which needs a machine to run the runner on.
notes: GitLab's own FAQ says the card is required 'if you choose to use GitLab.com shared runners', and shared runners are the only way to spend the 400 minutes without a self-managed runner. So the kind is `card`, with a USD 1.00 authorisation hold and release. Identity verification on the GitLab free tier is a risk-scored three-stage scheme, and it is documented; separately and unconditionally, the shared runners need a card. Not established: whether a new account from a given country lands in the medium-risk (phone) or high-risk (card) band, because the risk score is not published; and whether a debit or prepaid card passes the one-dollar authorisation, because no page says.

free_tier.stated: 'The base monthly compute quota is determined by your subscription tier. Free tier namespaces receive 400 compute minutes per month.' The pricing page repeats it as '400 compute minutes per month'. A compute minute is not a wall-clock minute: the usage formula is 'Job duration / 60 * Cost factor', and the default `small` Linux x86-64 runner has cost factor 1, so 400 compute minutes is 400 wall-clock minutes on the default shape and less on any larger one. The card requirement is the finding: 'credit/debit card details are required if you choose to use GitLab.com shared runners', verified with 'a one-dollar authorization transaction'.
free_tier.notes: 400 compute minutes at cost factor 1 is 6 hours 40 minutes a month, which is 0.22 hours a day. The card gate is on the shared runners specifically, not on the account.

retention.stated: 'Ephemeral runner VMs serve a single job and are deleted right after the job execution.' Nothing on the VM survives the job.
retention.notes: 0 means the VM is deleted at job end

egress.terms: not published on any page read: no egress quota, shaping tier or per-byte price is stated for GitLab.com hosted runners

identity_cost.detail: A card, for the thing this record is about. The account itself is free and the pricing page says 'No credit card required' for the Free plan, but the free compute minutes sit behind a card: 'credit/debit card details are required if you choose to use GitLab.com shared runners'. The card is verified by 'a one-dollar authorization transaction' and 'No charge will be made and no money will transfer', so the hold is USD 1.00 authorised and released, not captured. GitLab's identity-verification page adds a second, independent gate that is risk-scored: 'All users - Email verification. Medium-risk users - Phone number verification. High-risk users - Credit card verification.' Whether a new account lands in the medium or high band is not published. Debit acceptance is not stated on any page read; the pages say 'credit/debit card' without distinguishing.

shape.note: `saas-linux-small-amd64`, the default for untagged jobs. RAM and disk are the vendor's decimal GB, kept unconverted: 8 GB is about 7.5 GiB and 30 GB about 27.9 GiB. Quoted caveat: 'The storage is shared by the operating system, the container image with pre-installed software, and a copy of your cloned repository. This means that the available free disk space for your jobs to use is reduced.'

extras.price_arithmetic: 400 compute minutes / cost factor 1 = 400 wall-clock minutes a month on the 2 vCPU default, which is 6 h 40 min, or 0.22 h a day. 10 h a day x 30 = 300 h needs 18,000 compute minutes, 45 times the quota. 24/7 x 30 = 730 h needs 43,800 compute minutes, 110 times the quota. No USD figure is given because no per-minute price was read on a page.

concurrency.note: not published on any page read: no concurrent-job number for a Free namespace was found. The 400-minute monthly quota is the ceiling that matters at this size.

extras.units: RAM and disk are the vendor's decimal GB, kept unconverted. 8 GB reads as 8, 30 GB as 30.

binding_note: the card is what fails, not the quota: 400 compute minutes is small but the free minutes cannot be reached at all without a payment instrument on file, so the machine is behind an identity gate a user does not want to pass. Even past the card, 400 minutes a month is 6 hours 40 minutes.
